html:
Turkic herding tribes on the steppes between the Caspian and Aral seas and along the lower Syr Darya. The map shows them there in 1100.

In the 10th century their leader, the yabgu, ruled from Yangikent near the mouth of the Syr Darya. Many Oghuz became Muslim in this period, and Muslims came to call them Turkmen. One Oghuz clan, the Seljuks, rode south: they built the Seljuk Empire, took Baghdad in 1055 and beat Byzantium at Manzikert in 1071, which opened the way for Turks to settle in Anatolia.

The tribes left behind were pressed by the Kipchaks from the north and fell under Khwarazm to the south. The Oghuz are the ancestors of today's Turks, Azerbaijanis and the people of Turkmenistan. The map shows the same people around 900 as the Oghuz Turks.
sum: Turkic herding tribes on the steppes between the Caspian and Aral seas and along the lower Syr Darya. The map shows them there in 1100.
